svg.aria-label: B-tree versus B+ tree. In the original B-tree, every node, internal or leaf, stores keys together with their values or row pointers, so a key is stored only once wherever it lands. In a B+ tree, internal nodes hold only keys as signposts, so more of them fit per page and the tree is shallower; every value lives in the leaves, and the leaves are linked to their neighbours, so a range scan walks along the leaves without going back up the tree. Most databases use B+ trees and call them B-trees.
